speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. Can you describe your family history of bleeding disorders or bruising, and have you noticed any spontaneous bleeding from your gums or nose in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you ever experienced prolonged bleeding from minor cuts, or any episodes of blood in your urine or stool outside of dental procedures? Additionally, do you take any aspirin, ibuprofen, or other blood-thinning medications?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your family history of joint swelling and bleeding, this could be a Factor VIII deficiency (Hemophilia A). Have you noticed any deep muscle hematomas or spontaneous bleeding into your joints in the past?

REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Profile (PT, aPTT, INR) and Factor VIII activity level.

REQUEST IMAGES: None requested at this time.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Prothrombin_Time: 15 sec; Partial_Thromboplastin_Time: 60 sec; Factor VIII activity level: Not measured in provided dataset.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A.

The prolonged aPTT (60 sec) confirms a defect in the intrinsic pathway, and given the family history of joint swelling and male gender, this is consistent with Factor VIII deficiency. We have sufficient data to proceed with this diagnosis without further testing.
